title: 10 ways to have a better conversation
speaker: Celeste Headlee

sentences.en: All right, I want to see a show of hands: how many of you have unfriended someone on Facebook because they said something offensive about politics or religion, childcare, food?
sentences.zh: 好吧,我想看一场举手秀: 你们中有多少人没有在Facebook上交朋友, 因为他们说了一些关于政治或宗教, 儿童保育,食物的冒犯?

sentences.en: (Laughter) And how many of you know at least one person that you avoid because you just don't want to talk to them?
sentences.zh: 你们中有多少人知道至少有一个人被你避开 因为你只是不想和他们说话?

sentences.en: (Laughter) You know, it used to be that in order to have a polite conversation, we just had to follow the advice of Henry Higgins in "My Fair Lady": Stick to the weather and your health.
sentences.zh: 你知道,它曾经是,为了有礼貌的对话, 我们只需要遵循亨利・希金斯的建议 在"我的公平女士": 坚持天气和你的健康。

sentences.en: But these days, with climate change and anti-vaxxing, those subjects -- (Laughter) are not safe either.
sentences.zh: 但是,随着气候变化和反蒸发,这些主题 -- -- (笑声) -- -- 也不安全。

sentences.en: So this world that we live in, this world in which every conversation has the potential to devolve into an argument, where our politicians can't speak to one another and where even the most trivial of issues
sentences.zh: 因此,我们所生活的这个世界, 每一个对话都有可能演变成一个争论的世界, 我们的政治家无法相互交谈, 甚至是最微不足道的问题。

sentences.en: have someone fighting both passionately for it and against it, it's not normal.
sentences.zh: 有个人为它和反对它而激烈斗争,这不正常。

sentences.en: Pew Research did a study of 10,000 American adults, and they found that at this moment, we are more polarized, we are more divided, than we ever have been in history.
sentences.zh: Pew Research对一万个美国成年人进行了研究, 他们发现,现在,我们更两极分化了, 我们比历史上更分化了。

sentences.en: We're less likely to compromise, which means we're not listening to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们不太可能妥协, 这意味着我们不听对方。

sentences.en: And we make decisions about where to live, who to marry and even who our friends are going to be, based on what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 我们决定住在哪里,谁结婚, 甚至我们的朋友会是谁, 根据我们已经相信的东西。

sentences.en: Again, that means we're not listening to each other.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍,这意味着我们不听对方的话。

sentences.en: A conversation requires a balance between talking and listening, and somewhere along the way, we lost that balance.
sentences.zh: 谈话需要平衡 说话和听, 和某处沿途,我们失去了平衡。

sentences.en: Now, part of that is due to technology. The smartphones that you all either have in your hands or close enough that you could grab them really quickly.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为科技。智能手机要么在你们手中,要么在近距离,可以很快抓住它们。

sentences.en: According to Pew Research, about a third of American teenagers send more than a hundred texts a day.
sentences.zh: 根据皮尤研究,大约三分之一的美国青少年 每天发送100多条短信。

sentences.en: And many of them, almost most of them, are more likely to text their friends than they are to talk to them face to face.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人,几乎大多数, 更可能给他们的朋友发短信, 而不是当面和他们交谈。

sentences.en: There's this great piece in The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 大西洋有个很棒的作品

sentences.en: It was written by a high school teacher named Paul Barnwell.
sentences.zh: 是一位叫Paul Barnwell的高中老师写的

sentences.en: And he gave his kids a communication project.
sentences.zh: 他给了他的孩子一个沟通项目。

sentences.en: He wanted to teach them how to speak on a specific subject without using notes.
sentences.zh: 他想教他们如何在不使用笔记的情况下就某一主题发言。

sentences.en: And he said this: “I came to realize...” (Laughter) "I came to realize that conversational competence might be the single most overlooked skill we fail to teach.
sentences.zh: 他说:“我终于意识到......”(笑声) “我意识到,对话能力可能是我们未能传授的最为被忽视的技能。

sentences.en: Kids spend hours each day engaging with ideas and each other through screens, but rarely do they have an opportunity to hone their interpersonal communications skills.
sentences.zh: 孩子们每天花数小时通过屏幕交流思想,但他们很少有机会利用人际交流技巧。

sentences.en: It might sound like a funny question, but we have to ask ourselves: Is there any 21st-century skill more important than being able to sustain coherent, confident conversation?"
sentences.zh: 可能听起来像一个有趣的问题, 但我们必须问自己:是否有任何21世纪的技巧 比能够保持连贯和自信的对话更重要?”

sentences.en: Now, I make my living talking to people: Nobel Prize winners, truck drivers, billionaires, kindergarten teachers, heads of state, plumbers.
sentences.zh: 现在,我靠生活和人们交谈:诺贝尔奖得主、卡车司机、亿万富翁、幼儿园教师、国家元首、水管工。

sentences.en: I talk to people that I like. I talk to people that I don’t like.
sentences.zh: 我和我喜欢的人交谈,

sentences.en: I talk to some people that I disagree with deeply on a personal level.
sentences.zh: 我和一些我不同意的人谈 个人层面。

sentences.en: But I still have a great conversation with them.
sentences.zh: 但我还是和他们有很好的谈话

sentences.en: So I'd like to spend the next 10 minutes or so teaching you how to talk and how to listen.
sentences.zh: 所以我想花10分钟左右的时间 教你怎么说话 如何倾听

sentences.en: Many of you have already heard a lot of advice on this, things like look the person in the eye, think of interesting topics to discuss in advance, look, nod and smile to show that you're paying attention,
sentences.zh: 很多人已经听到很多关于这个的建议, 诸如看着人的眼睛, 想到有趣的话题 讨论提前,看,点头和微笑 显示你正在关注,

sentences.en: repeat back what you just heard or summarize it.
sentences.zh: 重复你刚才听到的 或者总结一下

sentences.en: So I want you to forget all of that. It is crap.
sentences.zh: 所以我要你忘掉这一切 简直是胡扯

sentences.en: (Laughter) There is no reason to learn how to show you're paying attention if you are in fact paying attention.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 没有理由学习 如何显示你正在关注 如果你事实上在关注。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) Now, I actually use the exact same skills as a professional interviewer that I do in regular life.
sentences.zh: (笑) (掌声) 现在,我实际上使用 完全相同的技能 一个专业面试员 我做在正常生活中。

sentences.en: So, I'm going to teach you how to interview people, and that's actually going to help you learn how to be better conversationalists.
sentences.zh: 所以,我要教你 如何采访人, 这实际上会帮助你 学习如何成为更好的对话者。

sentences.en: Learn to have a conversation without wasting your time, without getting bored, and, please God, without offending anybody.
sentences.zh: 学会谈话 不要浪费你的时间, 不要无聊, 和,请上帝,没有冒犯任何人。

sentences.en: We've all had really great conversations.
sentences.zh: 我们都有过非常好的谈话

sentences.en: We've had them before. We know what it's like.
sentences.zh: 我们以前有过,我们知道它是什么样子

sentences.en: The kind of conversation where you walk away feeling engaged and inspired, or where you feel like you've made a real connection or you've been perfectly understood.
sentences.zh: 那种谈话,你走开 感觉订婚和灵感, 或者你觉得你已经 做了一个真正的连接 或者你已经完全理解。

sentences.en: There is no reason why most of your interactions can't be like that.
sentences.zh: 没有理由,你的大部分互动 不能是这样的。

sentences.en: So I have 10 basic rules. I'm going to walk you through all of them, but honestly, if you just choose one of them and master it, you'll already enjoy better conversations.
sentences.zh: 所以我有10条基本规则。我会告诉你所有的规则, 但是老实说,如果你选择其中之一来掌握它, 你就会享受更好的对话。

sentences.en: Number one: Don't multitask. And I don't mean just set down your cell phone or your tablet or your car keys or whatever is in your hand.
sentences.zh: 第一:不要多任务。我不是说 放下你的手机或平板电脑 或你的车钥匙,或你手里的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, be present. Be in that moment. Don't think about your argument you had with your boss.
sentences.zh: 我是说,到时候就到,别跟你老板吵架

sentences.en: Don't think about what you're going to have for dinner.
sentences.zh: 别想晚餐要吃什么

sentences.en: If you want to get out of the conversation, get out of the conversation, but don't be half in it and half out of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想离开谈话, 离开谈话, 但不要是一半 和一半。

sentences.en: Number two: Don't pontificate. If you want to state your opinion without any opportunity for response or argument or pushback or growth, write a blog.
sentences.zh: 第二:不要自说自话。如果您想表达自己的观点而没有回应或争论的机会,或回击或成长的机会,请撰写博客。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, there's a really good reason why I don't allow pundits on my show: Because they're really boring.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 现在,有一个很好的理由 为什么我不允许 专家在我的节目: 因为他们真的很无聊。

sentences.en: If they're conservative, they're going to hate Obama and food stamps and abortion.
sentences.zh: 如果他们是保守派 他们会恨奥巴马 和食品券和堕胎。

sentences.en: If they're liberal, they're going to hate big banks and oil corporations and Dick Cheney.
sentences.zh: 如果他们是自由派 他们会讨厌大银行和石油公司 还有迪克·切尼

sentences.en: Totally predictable. And you don't want to be like that.
sentences.zh: 完全可以预测,你不想这样

sentences.en: You need to enter every conversation assuming that you have something to learn.
sentences.zh: 你需要进入每一个谈话 假设你有东西可以学习。

sentences.en: The famed therapist M. Scott Peck said that true listening requires a setting aside of oneself.
sentences.zh: 著名的治疗师M. Scott Peck说 真正的听力 需要抛开自己

sentences.en: And sometimes that means setting aside your personal opinion.
sentences.zh: 有时这意味着 撇开你的个人意见。

sentences.en: He said that sensing this acceptance, the speaker will become less and less vulnerable and more and more likely to open up the inner recesses of his or her mind to the listener.
sentences.zh: 他说,从这种接受感看,发言者将越来越脆弱,越来越有可能向听众敞开心扉。

sentences.en: Again, assume that you have something to learn.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍,假设你有东西要学

sentences.en: Bill Nye: "Everyone you will ever meet knows something that you don't."
sentences.zh: 比尔尼:"每个人都会知道一些你不知道的事情。"

sentences.en: I put it this way: Everybody is an expert in something.
sentences.zh: 我这样说,每个人都是某方面的专家。

sentences.en: Number three: Use open-ended questions. In this case, take a cue from journalists.
sentences.zh: 第三:使用开放式问题。在这种情况下,请从记者那里得到提示。

sentences.en: Start your questions with who, what, when, where, why or how.
sentences.zh: 问谁、什么、何时、何地、为何或如何。

sentences.en: If you put in a complicated question, you're going to get a simple answer out.
sentences.zh: 如果你提出一个复杂的问题, 你会得到一个简单的答案。

sentences.en: If I ask you, "Were you terrified?" you're going to respond to the most powerful word in that sentence, which is "terrified," and the answer is "Yes, I was" or "No, I wasn't."
sentences.zh: 如果我问你,"你害怕吗?" 你会对那个句子中最有力的词做出回应, 这个词是"恐怖", 答案是"是的,我是"或"不是"。

sentences.en: "Were you angry?" "Yes, I was very angry."
sentences.zh: "你生气了吗?" "是的,我很生气"

sentences.en: Let them describe it. They're the ones that know.
sentences.zh: 让他们描述,他们知道

sentences.en: Try asking them things like, "What was that like?"
sentences.zh: 试着问他们,"那是什么感觉?"

sentences.en: "How did that feel?" Because then they might have to stop for a moment and think about it, and you're going to get a much more interesting response.
sentences.zh: "感觉如何?" 因为那样的话 他们可能要停下来好好想想, 你会得到更有趣的回应。

sentences.en: Number four: Go with the flow. That means thoughts will come into your mind and you need to let them go out of your mind.
sentences.zh: 第四:顺着潮流走。这意味着思想会进入你的脑海, 你需要让他们离开你的脑海。

sentences.en: We've heard interviews often in which a guest is talking for several minutes and then the host comes back in and asks a question which seems like it comes out of nowhere, or it's already been answered.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到采访 客人在谈话几分钟 然后接待员回来 问一个似乎不知从何而来的问题

sentences.en: That means the host probably stopped listening two minutes ago because he thought of this really clever question, and he was just bound and determined to say that.
sentences.zh: 这意味着宿主可能两分钟前停止听 因为他想到了这个非常聪明的问题, 他只是被绑 并决心说。

sentences.en: And we do the exact same thing. We're sitting there having a conversation with someone, and then we remember that time that we met Hugh Jackman in a coffee shop.
sentences.zh: 我们做同样的事情。我们坐在那里 和某人交谈, 然后我们记得那次 我们在一家咖啡店里遇到了休·杰克曼。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And we stop listening. Stories and ideas are going to come to you.
sentences.zh: 我们不要再听了 故事和想法会来找你的

sentences.en: You need to let them come and let them go.
sentences.zh: 你得让他们来放他们走

sentences.en: Number five: If you don't know, say that you don't know.
sentences.zh: 第五点:如果你不知道,就说你不知道。

sentences.en: Now, people on the radio, especially on NPR, are much more aware that they're going on the record, and so they're more careful about what they claim to be an expert in and what they claim to know for sure.
sentences.zh: 现在,收音机上的人, 特别是NPR上的人, 更清楚他们正在录制, 所以他们更小心 他们声称什么是专家 和他们声称知道的肯定。

sentences.en: Do that. Err on the side of caution. Talk should not be cheap.
sentences.zh: 照做,小心一点,说话不便宜

sentences.en: Number six: Don't equate your experience with theirs.
sentences.zh: 第六点:不要把你的经验和他们的相等。

sentences.en: If they're talking about having lost a family member, don't start talking about the time you lost a family member.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在谈论失去一个家庭成员, 不要开始谈论 你失去一个家庭成员的时间。

sentences.en: If they're talking about the trouble they're having at work, don't tell them about how much you hate your job.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在谈论他们在工作时遇到的麻烦 别告诉他们你有多讨厌你的工作

sentences.en: It's not the same. It is never the same.
sentences.zh: 不一样的,从来就不一样

sentences.en: All experiences are individual. And, more importantly, it is not about you.
sentences.zh: 所有的经历都是个人经历 更重要的是,这与你无关

sentences.en: You don't need to take that moment to prove how amazing you are or how much you've suffered.
sentences.zh: 你不必花那个时间 来证明你有多了不起 或者你遭受了多少痛苦

sentences.en: Somebody asked Stephen Hawking once what his IQ was, and he said, "I have no idea. People who brag about their IQs are losers."
sentences.zh: 有人问过史蒂芬·霍金他的智商是什么 他说:“我不知道,那些吹嘘他们的智商的人都是失败者。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Conversations are not a promotional opportunity.
sentences.zh: 谈话不是一个促销机会。

sentences.en: Number seven: Try not to repeat yourself.
sentences.zh: 第七点:尽量不要重复。

sentences.en: It's condescending, and it's really boring, and we tend to do it a lot.
sentences.zh: 这是高贵的, 和它真的很无聊, 我们倾向于做它很多。

sentences.en: Especially in work conversations or in conversations with our kids, we have a point to make, so we just keep rephrasing it over and over.
sentences.zh: 特别是在工作谈话或和孩子谈话的时候, 我们有一个点, 所以我们只是不停地改写它。

sentences.en: Don't do that. Number eight: Stay out of the weeds.
sentences.zh: 别那么做,八号,别吃杂草

sentences.en: Frankly, people don't care about the years, the names, the dates, all those details that you're struggling to come up with in your mind.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说,人们不关心那些年, 名字,日期, 所有那些细节 你正在努力想出来的。

sentences.en: They don't care. What they care about is you.
sentences.zh: 他们不在乎,他们关心的是你

sentences.en: They care about what you're like, what you have in common.
sentences.zh: 他们关心你是什么样子,你有什么共同点。

sentences.en: So forget the details. Leave them out. Number nine: This is not the last one, but it is the most important one.
sentences.zh: 别管细节了,别管了,九号:这不是最后一次,但这是最重要的一次。

sentences.en: Listen. I cannot tell you how many really important people have said that listening is perhaps the most, the number one most important skill that you could develop.
sentences.zh: 听着,我无法告诉你有多少真正重要的人说过 倾听也许是最重要的, 最重要的技能,你可以发展。

sentences.en: Buddha said, and I'm paraphrasing, "If your mouth is open, you're not learning."
sentences.zh: 佛祖说,我在说, "如果你的嘴是张的, 你没有学习。"

sentences.en: And Calvin Coolidge said, "No man ever listened his way out of a job."
sentences.zh: 卡尔文·库立奇说,“没有人会听从他离开工作的方式。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Why do we not listen to each other?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不听对方的话?

sentences.en: Number one, we'd rather talk. When I'm talking, I'm in control.
sentences.zh: 第一,我们想谈谈 当我说话的时候,我控制了一切

sentences.en: I don't have to hear anything I'm not interested in.
sentences.zh: 我不需要听到我对什么不感兴趣

sentences.en: I'm the center of attention. I can bolster my own identity.
sentences.zh: 我是关注的焦点 我能加强我自己的身份

sentences.en: But there's another reason: We get distracted.
sentences.zh: 但还有另外一个原因:我们分心了。

sentences.en: The average person talks at about 225 word per minute, but we can listen at up to 500 words per minute.
sentences.zh: 平均人说话 大约225个字每分钟, 但我们可以听 最多500个字每分钟。

sentences.en: So our minds are filling in those other 275 words.
sentences.zh: 所以,我们的思想正在填满 以其他的275个字。

sentences.en: And look, I know, it takes effort and energy to actually pay attention to someone, but if you can't do that, you're not in a conversation.
sentences.zh: 听着 我知道 注意一个人 需要精力和精力 但如果你做不到的话 你就不是在谈话

sentences.en: You're just two people shouting out barely related sentences in the same place.
sentences.zh: 你们只是两个人 在同一地方大喊大叫

sentences.en: (Laughter) You have to listen to one another.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 你们必须互相倾听。

sentences.en: Stephen Covey said it very beautifully. He said, "Most of us don't listen with the intent to understand.
sentences.zh: Stephen Covey说得非常漂亮 他说,“我们中大多数人不是有意要理解的。

sentences.en: We listen with the intent to reply." One more rule, number 10, and it’s this one: Be brief.
sentences.zh: 我们听是为了回答。”还有一条规则,即第10条,那就是:简短。

sentences.en: Be interested in other people. You know, I grew up with a very famous grandfather, and there was kind of a ritual in my home.
sentences.zh: 我从小就跟一个很著名的爷爷一起长大

sentences.en: People would come over to talk to my grandparents, and after they would leave, my mother would come over to us, and she’d say, “Do you know who that was?
sentences.zh: 人们会来跟我的祖父母谈话, 离开后, 我妈妈会过来, 她说,“你知道那是谁吗?

sentences.en: She was the runner-up to Miss America. He was the mayor of Sacramento.
sentences.zh: 她是美国小姐的副手 他是萨克拉门托的市长

sentences.en: She won a Pulitzer Prize. He's a Russian ballet dancer."
sentences.zh: 她获得了普利策奖 他是俄罗斯芭蕾舞演员

sentences.en: And I kind of grew up assuming everyone has some hidden, amazing thing about them.
sentences.zh: 我长大了 假设每个人都有一些 隐藏,惊人的事情 关于他们。

sentences.en: And honestly, I think it's what makes me a better host.
sentences.zh: 说实话,我觉得这让我 成为更好的主人。

sentences.en: I keep my mouth shut as often as I possibly can.
sentences.zh: 我尽量闭口不说

sentences.en: I keep my mind open. And I’m always prepared to be amazed, and I'm never disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我敞开心扉。我总是准备感到惊讶,我从不失望。

sentences.en: You do the same thing. Go out, talk to people, listen to people, and, most importantly, be prepared to be amazed.
sentences.zh: 你做同样的事情。出去,和人交谈,听人说话, 最重要的是,准备感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Thanks. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢 (掌声)
